quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of
quests.question: Tensions were running high ___ the election, with both campaigns making last-minute appeals.
quests.targetSentence: Tensions were running high in the run-up to the election, with both campaigns making last-minute appeals.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In the run-up to' describes an extended period of building tension before an event, unlike 'on the eve of', which refers only to the night just before.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a whole period of building tension, not just the final night before.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in the run-up to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Tensions were running high in the run-up to the election, with both campaigns making last-minute appeals.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of
quests.question: The bride could hardly sleep from excitement ___ the wedding.
quests.targetSentence: The bride could hardly sleep from excitement on the eve of the wedding.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On the eve of' refers specifically to the night immediately before an event, distinct from the longer period described by 'in the run-up to'.
quests.nativeTip: This describes the single night immediately before an event, not a longer build-up period.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on the eve of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The bride could hardly sleep from excitement on the eve of the wedding.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of
quests.question: For weeks, the entire town seemed to buzz with anticipation ___ the championship game.
quests.targetSentence: For weeks, the entire town seemed to buzz with anticipation in the run-up to the championship game.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in the run-up to vs on the eve of
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In the run-up to' fits because 'for weeks' signals an extended lead-up period, not the single night described by 'on the eve of'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'for weeks' points to an extended period, not a single final night.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in the run-up to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'For weeks, the entire town seemed to buzz with anticipation in the run-up to the championship game.'

quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'with' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'All contractors must comply with local safety regulations at all times.'

quests.question: The design needed to conform ___ strict industry standards before approval.

quests.question: Employees are expected to adhere ___ the company's code of conduct.
